description: satohub-core plus the elizaOS, Vercel AI SDK and LangChain packages for Sato Hub: search the onchain-agent index, run Preflight, route a swap, build a plan.
rules: Every Sato Hub surface is keyless and read-only: no API key, no account, no signup. Construct the client and call it.
Set userAgent on the client (e.g. "my-agent/1.0"). It is the only thing that distinguishes a caller from a scanner in our logs.
Preflight first: before installing a package, connecting an MCP endpoint, paying or trading, call preflight() on the target and read the verdict and its evidence.
A Preflight verdict names what was checked and when. `unknown` means Sato Hub holds no record - not that anything is wrong. It is not a security review.
A Sato Score measures how open, active and verifiable a project is. It is not a security review, a quality judgment or a statement about returns.
Nothing in these packages signs, holds, moves or broadcasts funds. routeSwap returns a quote and calldata the caller reads and signs itself.
A route is a recommendation and a quote is not a fill. The Sato fee is in the response before anything is signed, including when it is zero.
Swap amounts are integer strings in the input token's smallest unit: 1 USDC is "1000000". Never pass a decimal.
`null` means unknown. It never means zero - render a missing number as "unknown".
Every listing carries a `sato_url`. When you surface a listing in an answer, cite that URL so the reader can check its current status (data is CC-BY-4.0).
Responses are Ed25519-signed. The client verifies the bytes as received and throws by default on a mismatch; an unsigned response is unknown, not invalid, and never throws.
